title: Improving Reproducibility to Meet Minimal Information for Studies of Extracellular Vesicles 2018 Guidelines in Nanoparticle Tracking Analysis
protocol: Maintain the microscope on an air table or a vibration-free table.
Keep extraneous vibrations to a minimum during experiments.
Set and maintain the laser module temperature at a constant 25 °C.
Use NTA-characterized diluents such as DPBS for all measurements.
Flush the laser module with characterized DPBS before analysis.
Factor contaminants in negative control DPBS into sample results if significant.
Store samples at 4 °C prior to evaluation.
Warm samples, standards, and diluents to room temperature for 30 min before analysis.
Evaluate sample and standards using Quick measurement to establish an appropriate dilution for NTA analyses.
Fill in all applicable fields within the Capture box of the SOP tab, including the dilution and diluent used.
Transfer 2 µL of the 50 nm standards into a twice-rinsed 15 mL conical tube containing 9,998 µL of 0.22 µm-filtered 10 mM potassium chloride/0.03% Tween 20 in ultrapure DW.
Store the diluted 50 nm standard at 4 °C for up to a year.
Transfer 30 µL of the 100 nm standards into a twice-rinsed 15 mL conical tube containing 9,970 µL of 0.22 µm-filtered 10 mM potassium chloride/0.03% Tween 20 in ultrapure DW.
Store the diluted 100 nm standard at 4 °C for up to a year.
Visually inspect the laser module and flow-cell cover windows for scratches or imperfections.
Clean both glass surfaces gently with a good quality lens cleaner and lens paper.
Ensure that the O-ring seal is properly seated in the groove of the flow-cell cover prior to assembly.
Place the flow-cell cover on the laser module, ensuring the electrical contacts are in the proper orientation.
Place the 4 spring-loaded thumbscrews through the flow-cell plate and engage the threads of the laser module but do not tighten individually.
Put uniform pressure down on the flow-cell cover, uniformly tighten the thumbscrews in an alternating diagonal manner until snug.
Only tighten the thumbscrews until finger-tight.
Do not overtighten.
Use a newly opened container of DPBS and aliquot into triple-rinsed 15 mL polypropylene tubes.
Flush two 1 mL tuberculin syringes with slip lock adaptors 3 times with 1 mL of DPBS to remove any particulate residues.
Remove and discard the plunger from the first tuberculin syringe.
Insert the removed plunger into the remaining port to serve as a voided diluent/sample reservoir.
Remove the plunger from the syringe.
Fill a second syringe with 1 mL of DPBS and attach it to the inlet port of the flow-cell cover.
Hold the laser module tilted, with the outlet syringe port elevated to allow air purging as DPBS is injected slowly into the laser module.
Inject 1 mL of air into the inlet port to flush remaining DPBS from the laser module.
Repeat flushing 2 more times using 1 mL of air each time.
Empty the laser module as completely as possible after the last flush.
Locate the laser module focus alignment guides on the arm of the microscope and align them using the focus knob.
Place the laser module in the grooved stage facing the microscope, gently sliding it as far to the right as possible.
Turn on the rocker switch on the laser control box.
Load the NTA software from the desktop.
Close and reopen the software if an error appears stating "Temperature H/W not found on COM3."
Click Start Camera under the Capture tab in the upper left corner box.
Adjust Camera Level to 14 to 16 to brighten the laser line and simplify particle identification and focus.
Divert the image from the camera to the eyepieces by moving the top slider on the left side of the headpiece.
Find the area of increased density, commonly referred to as the thumbprint.
Center and focus the thumbprint vertically in the field of view.
Darken the room to facilitate locating the thumbprint and focusing on the laser line.
Center the laser line in the field of view.
Move the top slider to divert light to the camera as observed on the computer screen.
Adjust the focus to sharpen the image of individual moving particles on the screen with the focus knob.
Draw up 1 mL of standard/sample/diluent into a rinsed 1 mL tuberculin syringe.
Attach the syringe to the inlet port of the flow-cell cover.
Advance the plunger until fluid is evident in the open syringe attached to the outlet port.
Move to the right of the laser line to an area of uniform number of particles.
If necessary, adjust the vertical orientation to center the horizontal bands of light.
Refocus until the highest number of particles are in view.
Ensure that for all subsequent measures, this position is maintained as closely as possible.
Adjust the Camera Level to the point that the Dark information symbol flashes intermittently on and off in the top right of the camera view.
Validate module calibration using size standards prior to sample analysis.
Warm diluted standards to room temperature for 30 min.
Briefly vortex the standards and load as described in section 7.
Perform sample NTA as described in section 10.
Set Capture duration to 30 s for Quick Measurement.
Accept the existing base filename or enter a new filename by clicking the ... tab for storage site.
Check the box for Target temperature and input the desired temperature.
Load the sample as previously described (step 7.1) and click Create and Run Script.
Flush the laser module 3 times if the number of particles is greater than 100.
Dilute the sample to the desired concentration range using the characterized diluent.
Load the properly diluted sample into the flushed laser module and run the Quick Measurement to verify the sample is within the acceptable range.
Set the duration to 30 or 60 seconds.
Enter a new filename by clicking the ... tab if desired.
Check the box for Target temperature and input the desired temperature.
Click Create Script to reuse this Standard Measurement.
Load the sample as described in section 7.
Fill out the fields in Set Report Details popup screen with operator information, sample description, dilution of the sample, and diluent used.
Click OK to initiate the script.
If Target temperature was selected, wait for the heater to stabilize the sample at the desired temperature for 5 seconds.
Prior to each video capture, inject approximately 0.05 mL of the sample into the laser chamber.
Allow the particles to come to "rest" before clicking OK.
Wait for a Settings Confirmation box to appear upon completion of the 5th video capture.
Set the Detection Threshold by noting the number of blue crosses marking particles on each frame as frames are advanced manually from the bottom of the screen.
Increase the Detection Threshold if there are more than 3-4 blue crosses per frame.
Click Settings OK when an acceptable Detection Threshold is set.
Wait for videos to be automatically processed and a histogram of results with a dialog box notification of completion to appear.
Save results by clicking Export once the Export Settings box appears.
Monitor storage requirements and transfer results to a secondary storage device as necessary.
Highlight all 5 capture videos listed in the Current Experiment for re-analysis.
Process selected files.
Wait for the Setting Confirmation box to appear.
Adjust the Detection Threshold to the desired level.
Click Setting OK.
Wait for videos to be automatically processed and a histogram of results and a dialog box notification of completion.
Click OK when the processing is complete.
Click Export Settings.
When re-analyzing recent samples, click the Export Results box in the Current Experiment.
Load NTA software from the desktop.
Click the Analysis tab in the lower middle panel.
Click Open Experiment and navigate to the desired .nano file.
Turn off the laser control box.
Flush the entire sample from the laser module and discard it properly.
Hold the laser module tilted with the open syringe port elevated to allow air to be purged from the chamber as DPBS is injected slowly into the laser module.
Flush the laser module until the sample is completely removed from the outlet syringe port.
Flush the remaining DPBS from the laser module and discard.
Repeat flushing 2 more times and empty the laser module as completely as possible after the last flush.
Put uniform pressure down on the flow-cell cover.
Uniformly loosen thumbscrews in an alternating diagonal manner until disengaged from threads.
Remove the thumbscrews and store them in the laser module case.
Remove the flow-cell cover from the laser module.
Clean both glass surfaces gently with a good quality lens cleaner and lens paper.
Visually inspect the laser module and flow-cell cover "windows" for scratches or imperfections following use and report to the supervisor.
Replace the laser module and flow-cell cover in their cases to prevent damage to glass surfaces during storage.
Vortex the sample prior to loading and record 5 x 60 s videos at Camera Level 12 and Detection Threshold Level 3.
Reanalyze these videos using Detection Thresholds 2 and 5.
Repeat video collections of the same sample at Camera Levels 13 and 14 and Detection Threshold Level 3.
Reanalyze these 2 additional videos using Detection Thresholds 2 and 5.
Repeat the entire process using 5 x 30 s videos in the SOP setting.
Vortex the sample and then simultaneously load and filter it (0.22 µm syringe filter) directly into the laser module.
Flush the syringe filter with two times its dead space volume to remove resident particulates before use.
Process filtered and unfiltered samples exactly as described in step 14.1.
